subject: math
title: Grade 1 Shapes: Sides, Corners and What Makes a Shape
seo_title: Grade 1 Shapes Worksheets: Defining Attributes, Composing Shapes and 3-D Shapes (1.G.A.1)
standard_text: Distinguish between defining attributes (e.g., triangles are closed and three-sided) versus non-defining attributes (e.g., color, orientation, overall size); build and draw shapes to possess defining attributes.
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 shapes worksheets with pictures: name circles, triangles, squares, rectangles, trapezoids and hexagons, count sides and corners, learn what matters (closed, straight sides) and what does not (color, size, turning), put shapes together, and find cubes, cones and cylinders in real life. 100 questions with answer key.
key_big: Sides and corners give a shape its name. Color, size and turning do not.
key_sub: A triangle is closed and has 3 straight sides. A turned square is still a square. Shapes can be put together: 2 triangles make a square, 2 squares make a rectangle.
body_html:
Know a shape by its sides and corners

A side is a straight line of a shape. A corner is where 2 sides meet. A corner is also called a vertex. Two or more are vertices.

To count, put your finger on one corner. Go around the shape. Count each corner once. Stop when you are back at the start.

ShapeNameSidesCornersRule
circle00round
triangle333 straight sides
square444 same sides, 4 square corners
rectangle444 square corners
trapezoid442 sides go the same way
hexagon666 straight sides
Example

A shape has 4 sides that are all the same length and 4 square corners. What is it?

4 same sides and 4 square corners make a square.

Answer: a square

What matters and what does not

A shape must be closed: the sides meet all the way around. The sides must be straight. The number of sides and corners gives the name.

Color, size and turning do not matter. A turned square is still a square.

Example

Is a small, blue, upside-down triangle still a triangle?

It is closed and has 3 straight sides. Size, color and turning do not matter.

Answer: yes

Put shapes together

You can put flat shapes together to make a new shape. The dashed lines show the parts.

Example

2 trapezoids are put together along the long sides. What shape do they make?

Each trapezoid is half of a hexagon. 2 halves make a whole.

Answer: a hexagon

Solid shapes

Some shapes are not flat. You can hold them. These are solid shapes (3-D shapes).

Solid shapeThings shaped like it
cubea game die, an ice cube, a toy block
rectangular prisma cereal box, a shoe box, a book
conean ice cream cone, a party hat
cylindera can of soup, a paper towel roll

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Calling a turned square a diamondTurning does not change a shape. It is still a square
Calling 3 lines with a gap a triangleA triangle must be closed
Thinking color or size changes the shapeCount the sides and corners. That gives the name
Counting 5 or 7 sides on a hexagonStart at one corner and stop when you are back there
Mixing up a cylinder and a coneA cylinder has 2 circles. A cone has 1 circle and a point
Calling a cube a squareA square is flat. A cube is a solid with square faces

faq.q: What are defining attributes of shapes in 1st grade?
faq.a: Defining attributes are what make a shape that shape: being closed, having straight sides, and the number of sides and corners. Color, size and turning are not defining attributes (Common Core 1.G.A.1).

faq.q: Is a square turned on its corner a diamond?
faq.a: It is still a square. It has 4 same sides and 4 square corners, and turning a shape never changes what it is.
Grade 1 students learn cubes, rectangular prisms, cones and cylinders. They name them and find them in real things, like a can (cylinder) or a die (cube).

faq.q: What shapes can you make with two triangles?
faq.a: Two same triangles can make a square or a rectangle when you put their long sides together. Six triangles can make a hexagon (Common Core 1.G.A.2).

items.q: What is the name of this shape?
items.e: It is round and has no sides and no corners. It is a circle.

items.q: What is the name of this shape?
items.e: It has 3 straight sides and 3 corners. It is a triangle.

items.q: What is the name of this shape?
items.e: It has 4 sides that are all the same length and 4 square corners. It is a square.

items.q: What is the name of this shape?
items.e: It has 4 sides and 4 square corners. 2 sides are long and 2 are short. It is a rectangle.

items.q: What is the name of this shape?
items.e: Count the sides: 6. A shape with 6 sides is a hexagon.

items.q: What is the name of this shape?
items.e: It has 4 sides. 2 sides go the same way, like train tracks, and one of them is longer. It is a trapezoid.

items.q: What is the name of this shape?
items.e: It is round and has no sides and no corners. It is a circle. Small or big, it is still a circle.

items.q: What is the name of this shape?
items.e: It has 3 straight sides and 3 corners. It is a triangle. It is turned, but it is still a triangle.

items.q: What is the name of this shape?
items.e: It has 4 sides that are all the same length and 4 square corners. It is a square. It is standing on a corner. Some people call it a diamond, but turning does not change the shape.

items.q: What is the name of this shape?
items.e: It has 4 sides and 4 square corners. 2 sides are long and 2 are short. It is a rectangle. It is standing up, but it is still a rectangle.

items.q: What is the name of this shape?
items.e: It has 4 sides. 2 sides go the same way, like train tracks, and one of them is longer. It is a trapezoid. It is upside down, but it is still a trapezoid.

items.q: What is the name of this shape?
items.e: Count the sides: 6. A shape with 6 sides is a hexagon. The sides are not all the same length. It is still a hexagon.

items.q: What is the name of this shape?
items.e: It has 3 straight sides and 3 corners. It is a triangle. It points down, but it is still a triangle.

items.q: What is the name of this shape?
items.e: It has 4 sides. 2 sides go the same way, like train tracks, and one of them is longer. It is a trapezoid. It does not have to look the same on both sides.

items.q: What is the name of this shape?
items.e: It has 4 sides and 4 square corners. 2 sides are long and 2 are short. It is a rectangle. It is tilted, but it is still a rectangle.

items.q: What is the name of this shape?
items.e: It has 4 sides that are all the same length and 4 square corners. It is a square. It is small, but it is still a square.

items.q: Which shape is a rectangle?
items.e: Shape B has 4 sides and 4 square corners. It is standing up, and that is fine. The slanted shape has 4 sides, but its corners are not square corners.

items.q: Which shape is a hexagon?
items.e: Shape D has 6 sides. A trapezoid is like half of a hexagon, but it has only 4 sides.

items.q: I have 6 sides. I have 6 corners. What shape am I?
items.e: A shape with 6 sides and 6 corners is a hexagon.

items.q: I am round. I have no sides and no corners. What shape am I?
items.e: A round shape with no sides and no corners is a circle.

items.q: How many sides does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one corner. Go around and count each side once: 3 sides.

items.q: How many corners does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one corner. Go around and count each corner once: 4 corners.

items.q: How many sides does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one corner. Go around and count each side once: 4 sides. Count the short sides too.

items.q: How many corners does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one corner. Go around and count each corner once: 3 corners. Turning a shape does not change how many corners it has.

items.q: How many sides does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one corner. Go around and count each side once: 6 sides. If you get 5 or 7, you missed a side or counted one twice.

items.q: How many corners does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one corner. Go around and count each corner once: 4 corners.

items.q: How many corners does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one corner. Go around and count each corner once: 6 corners. Turning a shape does not change how many corners it has.

items.q: How many sides does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one corner. Go around and count each side once: 4 sides.

items.q: How many sides does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one corner. Go around and count each side once: 4 sides. Turning a shape does not change how many sides it has.

items.q: How many corners does a circle have?
items.e: A circle is round all the way around. It has no straight sides, so it has 0 corners.

items.q: How many sides and corners does it have?
items.e: Count the sides: 6. Count the corners: 6. A flat shape with straight sides has the same number of each. If you get 7 corners, you counted the first corner again.

items.q: How many sides and corners does it have?
items.e: Count the sides: 3. Count the corners: 3. A flat shape with straight sides has the same number of each. If you get 4 corners, you counted the first corner again.

items.q: Shape A is big. Shape B is small. Which one has more corners?
items.e: Both are triangles. Each one has 3 corners. Size does not change the number of corners.

items.q: Which shape has 6 sides?
items.e: Shape A has 6 sides. It is a hexagon. The others have 4, 4 and 3 sides.

items.q: Which shape has 3 corners?
items.e: Shape C has 3 corners, so it is a triangle, even though it is turned. A circle has no corners.

items.q: Which shape has the most sides?
items.e: Shape B is the smallest shape, but it has the most sides: 6. Count the sides. Do not look at the size.

items.q: A shape has 4 sides. How many corners does it have?
items.e: Each side ends at a corner. A flat shape has the same number of corners as sides: 4.

items.q: A hexagon has 6 sides. A triangle has 3 sides. How many more sides does the hexagon have?
items.e: 6 − 3 = 3. The hexagon has 3 more sides.

items.q: How many corners do 2 triangles have in all?
items.e: Each triangle has 3 corners. 3 + 3 = 6 corners.

items.q: How many sides do a square and a triangle have in all?
items.e: A square has 4 sides. A triangle has 3 sides. 4 + 3 = 7 sides.

sets.title: Is it a triangle? What matters

items.q: Is this a triangle?
items.e: It is closed and has 3 straight sides. It is a triangle. Its size and color do not matter.

items.q: Is this a triangle?
items.e: Look at the corner with the gap. The sides do not meet, so the shape is open. A triangle must be closed.

items.q: Is this a triangle?
items.e: One side is curved. A triangle has 3 straight sides, so this is not a triangle.

items.q: Is this a triangle?
items.e: It has 3 straight sides and it is closed. It points down, but turning does not change the shape.

items.q: Is this a triangle?
items.e: It is small, but it is closed and has 3 straight sides. Small triangles are still triangles.

items.q: Is this a triangle?
items.e: Count the sides: 4. A triangle has only 3 sides. This shape is a trapezoid.

items.q: Which one is a triangle?
items.e: Shape C is closed and has 3 straight sides. One shape is open, one has a curved side and one has 4 sides.

items.q: Which one is NOT a triangle?
items.e: Shape A is open: 2 sides do not meet. The other three are closed with 3 straight sides. Their colors, sizes and turns do not matter.

items.q: Both shapes are triangles. What is different?
items.e: Both have 3 sides and 3 corners. Only the color, the size and the turn are different. These do not change the shape.

items.q: Is this a square?
items.e: It has 4 sides that are the same length and 4 square corners. It is a square standing on a corner.

items.q: Is this a rectangle?
items.e: It has 4 sides, but it leans over. Its corners are not square corners. A rectangle needs 4 square corners.

items.q: Is this a square?
items.e: There is a gap at one corner. The sides do not all meet, so it is open. A square must be closed.

items.q: Are shape A and shape B both hexagons?
items.e: Count the sides: A has 6 and B has 6. Both are hexagons. Size, color and side lengths do not matter.

items.q: Which one can change the name of a shape?
items.e: The name comes from the sides and corners. Color, size and turning never change the name.

items.q: Kai colors a triangle blue. What shape is it now?
items.e: Color does not change a shape. It still has 3 sides, so it is still a triangle.

items.q: Mia draws a big square. Luis draws a small square. Are they both squares?
items.e: Both have 4 same sides and 4 square corners. Size does not matter.

items.q: What does every triangle have?
items.e: Every triangle is closed and has 3 straight sides. It can point any way, and its sides can be different lengths.

items.q: Ava draws 3 straight lines. The ends do not all meet. Is it a triangle?
items.e: The lines must meet at every corner to make a closed shape. With a gap, it is not a triangle.

items.q: Ben turns a square on its corner. He says it is a diamond now. Is he right?
items.e: Turning does not change a shape. It still has 4 same sides and 4 square corners. It is a square.

items.q: What does every rectangle have?
items.e: Every rectangle is closed with 4 sides and 4 square corners. It can stand up, lie down or be any color.

items.q: This rectangle is made of 2 of which shape?
items.e: Look at the dashed line. Each part has 4 same sides and 4 square corners. 2 squares make the rectangle.

items.q: This square is made of 2 of which shape?
items.e: The dashed line goes from corner to corner. Each part has 3 sides. 2 triangles make the square.

items.q: Which 2 shapes make this rectangle?
items.e: The dashed line goes from corner to corner. Each part has 3 sides: 2 triangles.

items.q: How many triangles make this hexagon?
items.e: Count the triangles around the middle: 6. (3 is the number of dashed lines, not triangles.)

items.q: This hexagon is made of 2 of which shape?
items.e: Each half has 4 sides, and the long side is on the dashed line. 2 trapezoids make a hexagon.

items.q: How many triangles make this trapezoid?
items.e: Count the triangles: one points down in the middle, and one is on each side. That is 3.

items.q: Which shapes make this hexagon?
items.e: The bottom half has no lines inside: it is 1 trapezoid. The top half has 3 triangles.

items.q: How many small squares make this big square?
items.e: There are 2 small squares on top and 2 on the bottom. 2 + 2 = 4.

items.q: Which 2 shapes can make this rectangle?
items.e: Put 2 squares side by side and you get a long rectangle. Circles and hexagons do not fit together this way.

items.q: Which picture shows 2 triangles that make a square?
items.e: Picture D is a square cut from corner to corner, so it is 2 triangles. Another square is cut into 2 rectangles. One picture is a rectangle, and one is a triangle.

items.q: Put 2 squares side by side. Which shape do you get?
items.e: Shape B is a rectangle that is 2 times as long as it is tall. That is what 2 squares side by side make.

items.q: You put 2 triangles together. Which shape can you make?
items.e: Put 2 same triangles together along the long side and you can make a square. A hexagon needs more pieces, and a circle has no straight sides.

items.q: How many squares make this rectangle?
items.e: Count the parts between the dashed lines: 3 squares. There are 2 dashed lines, but 3 squares.

items.q: Owen has 2 trapezoids. He puts the long sides together. What shape does he make?
items.e: 2 trapezoids with the long sides together make a hexagon, like pattern blocks.

items.q: Maya makes hexagons. Each hexagon uses 2 trapezoids. She has 4 trapezoids. How many hexagons can she make?
items.e: 2 trapezoids make 1 hexagon. 2 more make another one. 2 + 2 = 4, so Maya can make 2 hexagons.

items.q: Which 2 shapes make this house?
items.e: The bottom has 4 same sides and square corners: a square. The roof has 3 sides: a triangle.

items.q: How many small triangles make this big triangle?
items.e: There is 1 at the top, 2 at the bottom corners and 1 in the middle that points down. 1 + 2 + 1 = 4.

items.q: This circle is made of 2 of which shape?
items.e: The dashed line cuts the circle into 2 same parts. Each part is a half circle.

items.q: How many more triangles do you need to finish the hexagon?
items.e: A hexagon needs 6 triangles. There are 4. 6 − 4 = 2 more.

items.q: Which shapes make this trapezoid?
items.e: The middle part has 4 same sides and square corners: 1 square. Each end has 3 sides: 2 triangles.

items.q: What is the name of this solid shape?
items.e: It is a solid, not flat. All its faces are the same square. It is a cube. A square is a flat shape.

items.q: What is the name of this solid shape?
items.e: It has a flat circle on the top and one on the bottom, with a round side. It is a cylinder.

items.q: What is the name of this solid shape?
items.e: It has 1 flat circle at the bottom and a point at the top. It is a cone. A triangle is flat.

items.q: What is the name of this solid shape?
items.e: It is shaped like a box. Some faces are long rectangles, so it is not a cube. It is a rectangular prism.

items.q: Which one is a cylinder?
items.e: Solid C has a flat circle on the top and on the bottom. The cone has only 1 circle and a point.

items.q: Which one is a cone?
items.e: Picture A has a point at the top and a circle at the bottom. One picture is a flat triangle, not a solid.

items.q: A can of soup is shaped like a ___.
items.e: A can has a flat circle on the top and the bottom. It is a cylinder.

items.q: An ice cream cone is shaped like a ___.
items.e: It has a point at the bottom and a circle at the top. It is a cone. A triangle is flat.

items.q: A game die is shaped like a ___.
items.e: A die has 6 faces that are all the same square. It is a cube. A square is only one flat face.

items.q: A cereal box is shaped like a ___.
items.e: A cereal box has big faces and thin faces, so it is not a cube. It is a rectangular prism.

items.q: A party hat is shaped like a ___.
items.e: A party hat is round at the bottom and has a point at the top. It is a cone.

items.q: A paper towel roll is shaped like a ___.
items.e: It is long and round, with a circle at each end. It is a cylinder.

items.q: Which one is a flat shape?
items.e: A circle is flat, like a drawing on paper. A cube, a cone and a cylinder are solid. You can hold them.

items.q: Which solid has a flat circle on the top and on the bottom?
items.e: A cylinder has 2 flat circles. A cone has only 1 circle and a point.

items.q: Which solid has a point at the top and a circle at the bottom?
items.e: A cone has 1 circle and a point. A cylinder has 2 circles and no point.

items.q: Ruby traces around the bottom of a can. What flat shape does she draw?
items.e: The bottom of a can is a flat circle, so Ruby draws a circle. The can itself is a cylinder.

items.q: Emma traces one face of a die. What flat shape does she draw?
items.e: Each face of a die is a flat square, so Emma draws a square. The die itself is a cube.

items.q: Noah puts 1 cube on top of another cube. What shape is the stack?
items.e: The stack is 2 times as tall as it is wide, so it is not a cube. It is a rectangular prism, like a box.

items.q: Omar has a can, a box, a die and a party hat. Which one is a cone?
items.e: The party hat has a point and a circle: a cone. The can is a cylinder, the box is a rectangular prism and the die is a cube.

items.q: Lily wants something that rolls smoothly across the floor. Which one should she pick?
items.e: A can is a cylinder. Its side is round, so it rolls smoothly. A box, a block and a book have flat faces and corners, so they do not roll smoothly.
